reading: The 6x6 block above the grey separator is a 3x3 pattern drawn at 2x scale; the 6x6 block of 2s below it is a mask. The output (18x18) puts one copy of the 3x3 pattern in each block whose mask cell is 2, other blocks empty.

slots.unit: top panel (above the separator row) downscaled by 2 to 3x3
slots.mask: bottom 6x6 panel; its non-background cells choose which 3x3 blocks get a copy

why: each 3x3 block (r,c) of the output equals the downscaled unit if mask(r,c) is fg, else all background
invariants: separator colour 5 never appears in the output

reading: Every isolated grey cell is replaced by a fixed 3x3 stamp centred on it: 5 at the corners, 1 at the edge midpoints, background in the centre.
why: one identical 3x3 copy [515/101/515] centred on every marker; the marker cell itself becomes background

reading: Each shape has one off-colour cell matching one of the coloured grid corners; the shape and that cell swap colours (shape takes the corner colour). In addition, all shapes keyed to a corner are overlaid (in the corner colour) as 5x5 boxes tucked into that corner.
verb: recolour by corner key and collect at corner

slots.keys: the non-background colours at the four grid corners
slots.subject: each object with one cell of a key colour
slots.recolour: object body -> key colour, key cell -> old body colour
slots.copy: union of all subject shapes for a key, drawn in the key colour with its bounding box flush in that key's corner

why: every object whose odd cell is corner colour k is swapped to colour k, and the k-corner 5x5 box is the overlay of those objects' boxes

reading: A lattice of framed boxes, most with a common interior colour and a few with rare interior colours. Between two cells of the same rare colour on one row or column, every background (0) cell is painted that rare colour; box cells in between stay.

new_rows.name: between_rare
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
rare(C) :- ccount(C, N), ccount(C1, N1), ccount(C2, N2), ccount(C3, N3), N1 > N, N2 > N, N3 > N, C1 < C2, C2 < C3.
between_rare(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y, X1, C), px(Y, X2, C), rare(C), X1 < X, X < X2.
between_rare(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y1, X, C), px(Y2, X, C), rare(C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.

why: every 0-cell lying between two cells of the same rare colour (fewer cells than at least three other colours) on its row or column takes that colour; nothing else changes

reading: A symmetric 16x16 pattern has some cells covered by colour-4 patches; restore them from the mirror-symmetric counterparts.
why: the output is symmetric left-right, top-bottom and about the diagonal; only the 4-cells change, each to its mirror cell's colour

reading: A cup shape sits on the bottom row with a centre of a second colour. From the two upper corners of the cup, diagonal lines in the centre colour run up and outward to the grid border.

slots.start: cells diagonally up-outward from the two end cells of the shape's top row
slots.direction: up-left from the left end, up-right from the right end
slots.colour: the inner (centre) colour of the bottom row

why: the added cells are exactly the two diagonal rays to the border, all in the inner colour

reading: Several identical framed panels each hold the same small shape at a height that changes by a constant step from panel to panel. The output is one panel with the shape moved one more step.

slots.panels: stripes cut by the full separator columns
slots.subject: the small shape in each panel
slots.step: constant vertical offset between consecutive panels (sign and size learned per input)
slots.output: one panel (frame + interior) with the shape at last position + step

why: the shape's row in the output panel continues the arithmetic sequence of its rows across the panels

reading: In every third column (columns 0, 3, 6, ...), colour 4 becomes 6.
why: every 4 cell whose column index is a multiple of 3 becomes 6; nothing else changes

reading: Left 4x4 panel of 1s with holes, right 4x4 panel with a coloured shape. If the shape exactly fills the holes, output the left panel with the shape dropped in; otherwise output the left panel unchanged.

slots.piece: right panel's coloured cells, same position
slots.condition: piece cells == base background cells exactly
slots.output: base with piece overlaid if condition holds, else base

why: output is the left panel; holes are filled by the right panel's colour only when the right shape equals the hole set

reading: Two 2-cells on the border define a straight line (row, column or diagonal). Along that line, 0 becomes 2 and 1 becomes 3.

new_rows.name: line22
new_rows.datalog:
end(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 2).
line22(Y, X) :- end(Y1, X1), end(Y2, X2), Y1 = Y2, X1 < X2, px(Y, X, C), Y = Y1, X1 < X, X < X2.
line22(Y, X) :- end(Y1, X1), end(Y2, X2), X1 = X2, Y1 < Y2, px(Y, X, C), X = X1, Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.
line22(Y, X) :- end(Y1, X1), end(Y2, X2), Y1 < Y2, D = Y2 - Y1, X2 = X1 + D, px(Y, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, K = Y - Y1, X = X1 + K.
line22(Y, X) :- end(Y1, X1), end(Y2, X2), Y1 < Y2, D = Y2 - Y1, X2 = X1 - D, px(Y, X, C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2, K = Y - Y1, X = X1 - K.

why: every cell strictly between the two 2-cells on their common line is recoloured 0->2, 1->3; nothing else changes
